description: Apply analytic geometry concepts, including norms, inner products, bilinear mappings, positive definite matrices, vector lengths and distances, angles, orthogonality, orthogonal matrices, orthogonal and orthonormal bases, orthogonal complements, and projections onto subspaces.

Use matrix decompositions, including determinants, traces, invertibility conditions, characteristic polynomials, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, eigendecomposition, diagonalization, singular value decomposition, and matrix approximation.

Apply vector calculus concepts, including univariate differentiation, Taylor expansion, partial derivatives, chain rule, gradients of multivariate functions, Jacobian matrices of vector-valued functions, matrix gradients with respect to vectors, backpropagation, higher-order partial derivatives, linearization, and multivariate Taylor series.

Apply probability and distribution concepts, including discrete and continuous random variables, probability mass functions, probability density functions, cumulative distribution functions, conditional probability, multiplication rule, total probability rule, Bayes' theorem, means, variances, covariance, correlation, independence, and Gaussian distributions with marginals, conditionals, sums, and products.
Solve continuous optimization problems using gradient descent for local minima, Lagrange multipliers for constrained extrema, convex optimization concepts, and linear programming.

Apply linear regression concepts, including problem formulation, parameter estimation, maximum likelihood estimation, maximum a posteriori estimation, generalization error, overfitting, and Bayesian linear regression.

Apply dimensionality reduction with PCA, including covariance matrices, maximum-variance subspaces, principal subspace bases, low-rank matrix approximation, PCA in high dimensions, projection perspectives, eigenvector computation, and key practical PCA steps.

Apply support vector machine classification, including separating hyperplanes, primal and dual SVM formulations, kernel-based nonlinear classifiers, and numerical approaches for finding optimal SVM solutions.
Develop group-working skills and self-discipline for applied mathematics and machine learning project contexts.
